aspects.says: &, ^ and | bind looser than == and !=, so a mask test needs parentheses; on ints the unparenthesised form doesn't compile, on booleans it compiles with another meaning.
basis: section:Bit Operators Bind Looser Than ==, and an int Shift Counts Only to 31
aspects.reason: the compiler rejects the unparenthesised int form, so there is no wrong solution that compiles to plant; the any-versus-all mask test that follows it is graded by feature-mask

aspects.says: + groups left to right, and once its left operand is a String it concatenates, so "s" + 1 + 2 is "s12" while 1 + 2 + "s" is "3s".
basis: section:Precedence and Associativity Group an Expression; Its Operands Still Run Left to Right

aspects.says: Integer / discards the fraction, so a percentage computed as part / whole * 100 is 0 until part reaches whole; multiplying first keeps it.
basis: section:Integer Division Truncates Toward Zero, and % Takes the Sign of the Dividend

aspects.says: Precedence decides grouping, not the order of evaluation: Java evaluates the left operand fully before the right one, including an array index on the left of an assignment.
basis: section:Precedence and Associativity Group an Expression; Its Operands Still Run Left to Right

aspects.says: (mask & set) != 0 asks whether any bit of the set is on and (mask & set) == set whether all are; mask & ~set clears the bits while ^ flips them.
basis: section:Bit Operators Bind Looser Than ==, and an int Shift Counts Only to 31

aspects.says: x++ evaluates to the old value and increments as a side effect, so x = x++ leaves x unchanged.
basis: section:Precedence and Associativity Group an Expression; Its Operands Still Run Left to Right

aspects.says: % takes the sign of the dividend, so a negative left operand gives a negative remainder and a negative index; Math.floorMod takes the divisor's sign.
basis: section:Integer Division Truncates Toward Zero, and % Takes the Sign of the Dividend

aspects.says: An int shift uses only the low five bits of its distance and a long shift the low six, so 1 << 35 is 8 even when assigned to a long; the left operand must be a long.
basis: section:Bit Operators Bind Looser Than ==, and an int Shift Counts Only to 31

aspects.says: && and || skip their right operand when the left decides the result, so && can guard a null check; & and | evaluate both and throw on the null.
basis: section:&& and || Skip Their Right Operand; & and | Always Evaluate Both

aspects.says: A call on the right of || or && is skipped once the left decides, so changed = changed || apply(x) stops applying after the first change.
basis: section:&& and || Skip Their Right Operand; & and | Always Evaluate Both

aspects.says: Integer / rounds toward zero, so a small negative offset falls in the same bucket as a small positive one; Math.floorDiv rounds toward negative infinity.
basis: section:Integer Division Truncates Toward Zero, and % Takes the Sign of the Dividend

aspects.says: >> copies the sign bit and >>> fills with zeros, so (low + high) >>> 1 halves an overflowed sum correctly where / 2 stays negative.
basis: section:Bit Operators Bind Looser Than ==, and an int Shift Counts Only to 31
aspects.reason: a reader who gets the midpoint right will usually write low + (high - low) / 2, which the page also gives, so a test cannot tell whether the unsigned shift was understood; the page shows the run
